items.title: South Africa Already Upgraded by Bond Market as Rating Firms Lag
items.author: Matthew Hill and Alexander Parker
items.content: <article>South African authorities are focused on hitting budget targets rather than pleasing credit-rating firms, according to the government’s top finance official — and the reward is a bond market that’s already pricing the country’s debt as investment grade.</article>

items.title: Zimbabwe’s VFEX Plans $5 Billion Market Value, Venture Board for Mining
items.author: Godfrey Marawanyika
items.content: <article>Zimbabwe’s dollar-denominated stock exchange plans to increase its market value by 25% over the next year as it rolls out new products, including a venture board to help junior mining and exploration companies raise capital.</article>

items.title: Iran Wants to Bar US, Israeli Ships From Hormuz in Deal
items.content: <article>Iran will seek to bar US and Israeli ships from the Strait of Hormuz and require compensation from hostile countries before they’re allowed to sail through it, according to local media reports on a proposed Iran-Oman deal. Bloomberg's Abeer Abu Omar has the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>

items.title: Hong Kong's Iconic Diners Go Global
items.content: <article>Hong Kong has exported everything from cinema to finance. Now, its iconic cha chaan teng diners are going global too. Mary Hui explains how these humble cafes have become a symbol of culture, migration and identity. (Source: Bloomberg)</article>
